title: A job application, from draft to outcome
summary: The eight statuses an application record can hold, the pipeline the Career workspace presents, and the three that close it. The enum is enforced; the ordering is not.
note: Read the arrows as the route the interface offers, not as a rule the server keeps. An application is an ordinary graph node: its status is a required enum on `applicationProps` (packages/core/src/schema/node-props.ts:192), and the only writer is the generic node patch (apps/api/src/routes/v1/nodes.ts:223), which validates the value against the enum and nothing else. There is no transition table, no guard, and no server-side rejection of a jump from `draft` straight to `accepted`. `GET /applications` is a read-only projection over the graph (apps/api/src/routes/v1/applications.ts:272) and never writes a status. Two facts follow. First, the ordering shown here lives entirely in the browser, as `PIPELINE_STAGES` and `OUTCOME_STAGES` (apps/web/src/routes/career/application-view.ts:3-4). Second, a legacy record with no readable status is read as `draft` rather than failing the workspace (apps/api/src/routes/v1/applications.ts:67). Note also that a job posting carries its own separate status vocabulary — watching, interested, applied, closed, passed (packages/core/src/schema/node-props.ts:185) — which this machine does not govern; and that `CAP-CAREER` is the capability these records belong to, for which docs/registry/requirements.json records no requirement at all.

states.label: Draft
states.note: The record exists but nothing has been sent. Also the fallback the API reads for a record whose stored status it cannot parse (apps/api/src/routes/v1/applications.ts:67), so a pre-schema bundle stays readable instead of breaking the whole workspace.

states.label: Applied
states.note: Submitted. `applied_on` is a separate optional date field, not derived from the status, so the two can disagree.

states.label: Screening
states.note: Recruiter or resume screen. Counted as active: it is not in `CLOSED_STATUSES`.

states.label: Interview
states.note: Interview rounds are separate `interview` nodes joined by `INTERVIEW_FOR` edges, each with its own outcome enum — scheduled, passed, failed, pending, cancelled (packages/core/src/schema/node-props.ts:228). A failed round does not move the application; a person does.

states.label: Offer
states.note: An offer is on the table. Still open — the decision has not been recorded.

states.label: Accepted
states.note: Closed. Counted out of `active` and out of `needs_attention`, so an overdue next step on an accepted application stops nagging.

states.label: Rejected
states.note: Closed by the other side. Sorted below every open application in the list.

states.label: Withdrawn
states.note: Closed by you. The enum does not distinguish withdrawing before a reply from withdrawing after an offer.

transitions.label: Submit the application
transitions.note: Set on the record through the application form's status select; `applied_on` and `next_step_date` are filled in the same dialog.

transitions.label: They replied and a screen is scheduled
Passed the screen; interview rounds begin
Another round
transitions.note: Nothing in the status changes between rounds. The round is a new `interview` node joined by an `INTERVIEW_FOR` edge; the dossier lists them in stage order and surfaces the next one whose outcome is not cancelled, passed or failed.

transitions.label: Accept the offer
transitions.note: The only transition into `accepted` the interface's own stage ordering suggests.

transitions.label: Rejected without a screen
transitions.note: `rejected` is one of the three statuses the API treats as closed, which is what removes it from the active count and the attention count.

transitions.label: Offer pulled
transitions.note: The enum has no separate value for a rescinded offer; `rejected` absorbs it.

transitions.label: Decline the offer
transitions.note: Declining and withdrawing share one value, so the list cannot tell an offer you turned down from an application you dropped.
